ROLE
You are a senior frontend engineer and product designer. Build a production-quality,
pure-frontend Test Automation Control Center for an existing Playwright suite.
It must run in a web browser with no backend, no build step and no server.

DELIVERABLE
- One self-contained index.html (HTML + CSS + JS inline). No server, no build step.
- Allowed CDNs only (pin exact versions): Lucide icons, Chart.js, GSAP (animations),
  canvas-confetti, JSZip. No other external requests.
- Must work offline after first load, responsive (desktop first, usable at 768px),
  light and dark theme via CSS variables, keyboard accessible, prefers-reduced-motion respected.

HARD RULE: NO NATIVE UI
Do not use native alert/confirm/prompt, <select>, <input type=checkbox/radio/date/range>,
native title tooltips, or default scrollbars. Build custom components:
dropdown (searchable, multi-select with chips), checkbox, toggle switch, radio cards,
segmented control, modal, drawer, tooltip, toast, context menu, date-range picker,
progress ring, skeleton loader, tabs, accordion. All icons are Lucide icons, never emoji.

THE SUITE (seed this exact catalogue as data, grouped by project → file → test)
Project "unit" (offline, non-mutating)
  tests/unit/dates.spec.ts — Days unit expectedRange cases; N-day windows are exactly N days;
  weeks never overlap; rolling 3-month options = check-spec; Weeks/Months units;
  availableHours: Oct 2026 = 198 h, D-03 overrun = 225 h, custom Oct 12–Nov 6 = 180 h,
  holidays excluded, fmt/parse round-trip.
Project "workload" (Admin session, mutating, runs serially)
  views-favourite-refresh.spec.ts — WL-G-01 All Users loads every user; WL-G-02/03 favourite
  add/remove; WL-G-04 refresh keeps selections.
  edit-combinations.spec.ts — step 1 description + every view type; step 2 every Relative
  option per unit (Days/Weeks/Months); step 2 Custom range per unit; step 3 view style;
  step 3 every data label per view type; step 3 Show Options (Timeline).
  defects.spec.ts (@defect) — WL-D-02, WL-D-03, WL-D-04, WL-D-05, WL-D-06.
Project "permissions" — SET-01 profile grid; per profile (none, view, manage, delete, full,
  projonly, globonly): G-01/03 open, G-04 Create option, G-05 seed view menu,
  G-06 API edit, G-07 API create; ISO user rows render.
Tag each test: project, file, tags (@defect, mutating, offline), est. duration, and whether it
needs a saved login for a profile.

SCREENS
1. Run Configuration (left panel)
   - Environment dropdown: Local (projects.localzoho.com), Staging, Production. Each has baseURL
     and portal; add/edit environments in a modal. Show a coloured env badge everywhere.
   - Browser selection as icon radio cards: Chromium, Chrome, Firefox, WebKit, Edge, with
     headed/headless toggle, viewport preset dropdown (1366×860 default), workers (locked to 1
     with an explanatory tooltip for mutating projects), retries, timeout.
   - Suite options mapped to the real .env: ZP_WEEK_START (Sunday/Monday segmented),
     ZP_EXPECT_KNOWN_DEFECTS toggle, ZP_SEED_VIEW_PREFIX, RUN_ID (auto QA-WL-<timestamp>),
     ZP_ALLOW_PROFILE_CHANGES toggle (shows a red warning modal before enabling),
     saved-login status per profile (green/grey chips).
   - Trace / screenshot / video mode dropdowns (off, on, retain-on-failure).
   - "Copy CLI command" button that generates the exact npx playwright command
     (--project, --grep, --headed, env vars) for the current selection. Toast on copy.
2. Test Explorer (centre)
   - Tree with checkboxes: project → file → test, live search, filter chips
     (status, tag, project), select all / none / failed only.
   - Every test row: Run button (run individually), status icon, last duration, flaky badge,
     context menu (run, run with trace, view last result, copy grep command).
   - Toolbar: Run selected, Run all, Run failed, Run @defect, Stop, Pause/Resume.
3. Live Run view
   - Overall progress ring + linear bar with percent (animated count-up), tests passed/failed/
     skipped/remaining counters, elapsed time, ETA / time left (calculated from est. durations,
     corrected by a moving average of actual durations), current test name, current step.
   - Per-test progress bars in a queue list; the running test shows its live step log
     (Action · Expected · Actual · layer: header / grid / API / reopened form) streaming in
     a terminal-style panel with auto-scroll and a "pin" toggle.
   - Mutating tests show an amber "portal state will be snapshotted and restored" chip and a
     final "Restore verified" step.
   - Toasts: run started, test failed (with "View bug" action), run finished, run stopped.
4. Bugs
   - A bug is created for every failed test. ID continues the WL-D-nn series.
   - Each bug has: severity (Critical/Major/Minor/Cosmetic dropdown), functional vs cosmetic,
     environment, browser, timestamp, numbered reproduction steps, Expected vs Actual,
     evidence from at least two layers (header, grid, API params, reopened form),
     screenshot, and video recording.
   - Seed the known defects WL-D-01 to WL-D-06 with realistic steps and expected/actual text
     taken from the catalogue above.
   - Statuses: New → Confirmed / Not reproduced / Refined, with a re-verify button that
     re-runs the linked test. Export a bug as Markdown or copy it to clipboard.
5. Reports
   - Run history list with diff between two runs (new failures, fixed, still failing).
   - Animated dashboard: KPI cards with count-up, pass-rate donut, duration-per-test bar chart,
     pass/fail trend line across runs, per-browser and per-environment breakdown,
     slowest 5 tests, flaky tests, defect severity chart.
   - Animations: staggered card entrance, chart draw-in, confetti on 100% pass,
     a subtle shake on the failure KPI, smooth tab transitions.
   - Export: report as a standalone HTML file, results as JSON and JUnit XML, all bugs as a ZIP.

EXECUTION MODES (be honest in the UI about which mode is active)
A) Simulation mode (default, works with no backend): a deterministic engine runs the
   catalogue with realistic durations and step logs. Known defects fail and everything else
   passes, with a seeded random-failure option. Clearly label the run banner "Simulated".
B) Import mode: drag-and-drop or folder-pick the real Playwright output
   (reports/results.json, junit.xml, test-results/** with *.webm videos, screenshots,
   trace.zip). Parse the Playwright JSON reporter schema (suites → specs → tests → results
   → attachments) into the same data model so Explorer, Bugs and Reports show real data,
   and real videos play in the bug view.
C) Adapter interface: isolate all execution behind
   runner.start(config, tests) / runner.on('progress'|'step'|'result'|'end') / runner.stop()
   so a WebSocket runner can replace the simulator later without UI changes.
   Ship a stub WebSocketRunner with the expected message schema documented in a comment.

VIDEO RECORDING
- In simulation mode, render each test's run as an animated "browser replay" on a canvas:
  a mock Workload Report page with a cursor, highlighted elements, the step caption, and a
  red failure overlay. Record it with the MediaRecorder API into a real WebM.
- Bug view: custom video player (no native controls) with play/pause, scrubber, speed
  (0.5×/1×/2×), step markers on the timeline that jump to each step, download, fullscreen.
- In import mode, use the Playwright video attachment instead.

DATA AND PERSISTENCE
- One state store. Persist environments, settings, run history and bugs to localStorage
  (wrap every access in try/catch and fall back to memory). Store videos as object URLs
  for the session; warn that they disappear on reload unless exported.
- Settings page: theme, toast position, sound on finish, clear data (custom confirm modal).

QUALITY BAR
- Visual direction: modern dark-first QA console (think Linear / Vercel), Inter font with a
  system fallback, 8px spacing grid, glassy panels, status colours
  pass #22c55e, fail #ef4444, skip #a3a3a3, running #3b82f6, flaky #f59e0b.
- Empty, loading (skeletons) and error states for every panel.
- No console errors. Clean code split into clearly commented modules inside the one file:
  store, catalogue, runner, recorder, importer, components, views, charts.

ACCEPTANCE CHECKS (verify before finishing)
1. Run one test individually → progress, ETA, step log, result, toast.
2. Run all on Firefox + Staging → env/browser shown on run, bugs and report.
3. A failed test has steps, expected/actual, two evidence layers, and a playable video.
4. The report animates, exports HTML/JSON/JUnit, and compares two runs.
5. Search the code: no native select, checkbox, radio, date input, alert or confirm.
6. Importing a sample Playwright results.json populates every view.
Then list anything you could not complete and why.
